# 1297-ranking-score — Rank candidates by their interpolated score

- **Status:** accepted · 2026-10-26 UTC · issue #1297.
- **Disposition:** POLICY-ACCEPTED (never MATCH).
- **Policy limb:** language artefact, limb 3 under #1303 / merged #1304. A language-neutral ranking requirement does not name frequency conversion. This is neither a transcendental precision difference (a), a memory-safety substitution (b), nor an abort refusal (c).
- **Pin:** libpinyin 2.11.92 at 074a2219; tree read: a checkout at 074a2219 whose cited blobs were hashed against the pin. Reference GLib 2.84.4; both facades; backend-independent logic (bdb gate).
- **Pin derivation:** `pinyin.cpp:1811-1866,1918-1921,2128-2138,2440-2445`; `zhuyin.cpp:1237-1287,1351-1357`. Existing binary evidence for the conversion instructions is retained in [921-927-glib-sorts.md](921-927-glib-sorts.md).
- **Rust counterpart:** `crates/oxpinyin-engine/src/session/mod.rs` and `crates/oxpinyin-capi/src/predict.rs`; affected C entry points: guess_candidates, guess_candidates_before_cursor, guess_candidates_after_cursor, guess_predicted_candidates, guess_predicted_candidates_with_punctuations.
- **Forward trace:** C facade parse / validation -> engine session matrix and dictionary/model lookups -> trellis or candidate construction -> ranking / dedup -> sentence and candidate getters. Predicted variants collect prefix/bigram rows, use the same score and ordering, then prepend punctuation where requested.
- **Backward trace:** ordinary and offset candidate windows, the before-cursor zhuyin path, prefix-seeded and constrained sentence guesses, addon and LONGER candidates, and plain / punctuation prediction are included as applicable. Both facades delegate decoding and window ranking to the engine. Backend adapters provide counts and items; they do not choose these orders. The fallback model without real unigrams uses its existing cost path. Punctuation itself is prepended rather than frequency-sorted.
- **Input partition / affected inputs:** Valid small unequal frequencies no longer tie because of integer storage; invalid-range lambda values keep a deterministic total order of their scores. Zero-total refusal and logging remain at their current callers; the pure score helper retains the zero-total fallback needed by non-facade sessions.
- **Difference:** The pin scales the interpolated score by 2^24 and stores it in guint32. Unequal small scores collapse to integer ties; negative, excessive and nonfinite scores undergo compiler-dependent conversion. Rust compares the unscaled interpolated score with a total order. One shared score implementation supplies ordinary, addon, longer and predicted candidates and their text deduplication winners. The product's interpolation, dynamic-adjust gate and 0.1 bigram discount remain.
- **Why accepted:** the replaced operation is a language/library artefact classified by the pinned #1306 Phase 2 plan. Rust expresses the specified product ranking directly. No product comparator constant, limit, option meaning or interpolation rule is replaced.
- **Contract preserved:** C ABI/layout, exported symbols, real GArray allocation and g_free ownership/lifetime are unchanged. System and user file formats and data ownership are unchanged. Process-wide side effects and diagnostics are unchanged. The documented list/sentence order and text-dedup winner are the affected observables; selecting a changed row naturally selects its existing token path.
- **Complexity:** Score construction remains O(n), sort O(n log n), dedup O(n) expected time. Shared fixed-width score values replace fixed-width integer keys.
- **Tests:** existing contract-diff driver, issues #921/#927/#594/#1275, table-conf-lambda, prediction and punctuation cases; n-best choose/train differentials. Changed cases receive exact POLICY-ACCEPTED observations, retained controls remain MATCH. A named mutation verifies the selection. No new generic driver is required.
- **Prior rulings:** none reversed. LC_NUMERIC is unchanged.
- **Evidence:** BDB setup uses `tools/cloud/setup.sh --cells bdb --cache-dir <private-cache>`; reproduction methods are below; retained results and limitations are recorded in PR #1314. Captures stay local and disposable.
- **Conclusion:** accepted under the maintainer's explicit Phase 2 instruction and language-artefact policy, 2026-10-26 UTC.

## Corpus and benchmark reproduction

This record documents the candidate pass at `9e2ef151` and the benchmark
at `4b5c3844`, based on `01475357`, before the maintainer parked #1314 to
merge last. Production sources and
retained binaries are unchanged by the subsequent documentation revision.
These commands document earlier executions; they are not instructions to
run another campaign while the PR is parked. The final combined-main pass
requires the maintainer's instruction. Results and limitations remain in
[PR #1314](https://github.com/shenghaoc/oxpinyin/pull/1314).

### Candidate-score isolation

The single actual-facade pass ran at tree
`b249a6d49ce7d1d9bd114fbaef7ebd0c75270c31`. Only benchmark storage/tooling
changed afterward; the production crate tree remained
`7a38cddc9e9c164f05331606988e114175c6f700`, as did the measured shipping
objects. The earlier selection experiment did not retain complete candidate
windows, so this was the authorized fallback.

The existing `tools/bisection/contract-diff.py --candidate-score-attribution` entry point parses the same nine committed corpus strata through both actual full-pinyin C entry points, then reads complete candidate windows at offset zero (`pinyin_guess_candidates`, sort `0x1c`; `zhuyin_guess_candidates_after_cursor`). It does not guess a sentence, rejects sentence candidates, and refuses any parse spanning 256 bytes or more. Thus tournament/tail ordering and byte-span narrowing cannot contribute. With the unchanged verified model’s λ = 0.312699, valid unigram counts and options `0x18a` (DYNAMIC_ADJUST clear), the old scaled nonnegative keys remain below 2²⁴: unsigned subtraction cannot reverse a pair, and both sorting algorithms are stable. The observed candidate differences therefore isolate score scaling/truncation and the associated score-based deduplication. Parse/return fields, corpus digests and library hashes are checked unchanged. This pass covers ordinary offset-zero windows with an empty user profile; it does not measure prediction, other cursors or a Bopomofo corpus. Complete windows were not retained from the earlier sentence experiment, so this was the one authorized fallback pass.

Reproduce this candidate pass after provisioning (BASE and PR are the corresponding BDB shipping prefixes):

```sh
just heavy -- uv run --no-project --managed-python python tools/bisection/contract-diff.py \
  bdb "$PIN" "$PR/lib/libpinyin.so" --zhuyin-so "$PR/lib/libzhuyin.so" \
  --base-pinyin-so "$BASE/lib/libpinyin.so" --base-zhuyin-so "$BASE/lib/libzhuyin.so" \
  --candidate-score-attribution
```

### Review correction: unconditional final-pass recount

**FINALPASSRECOUNT — split required.** The old candidate output counted every
changed sequence as an order change, even when candidate rows changed. The
reported 8,575 pinyin / 8,486 zhuyin “order change” counts and their unsplit
first/top-five/largest-position figures are superseded; complete windows
were not retained, so no split is inferred from them.

The existing driver now compares full row **multisets** before sequences.
Equal multisets with different sequences increment `order_only`; unequal
multisets increment `row_set` (including changed duplicate multiplicities).
Each class separately reports changed windows, first-candidate and top-five
counts, and the largest changed one-based position. Unchanged windows do
not enter either class. Attribution rejects planning/listing, ordinary-case,
other campaign and unsupported modifier options before dispatch or artifact
inspection.

The final pass must recount both classes for both actual facades
**unconditionally**, replacing the earlier condition tied to a merged
candidate-ranking change. No recount is authorized while #1314 is parked;
it waits for the maintainer's final-pass release. These review fixes do not
supply any new corpus figures.

### Bound native benchmark

Record mode used 178 entries derived by the bench itself, containing the
complete base/PR/pin input observations and protected envelopes. The binding
names base commit `01475357ab03f74951fce25983193395b97eef3c` and PR tree
`cf3830ff303f121c1fd03a77f477601051ea5d8a`, plus library/worker and input
identities. The registration is a private run input, never a committed
allowlist or published capture. Streaming compressed entries shares identical
immutable file bytes while keeping complete observations in each entry.
PR/control observations, units, persistence operations, native file checks
and stderr remain strict; unregistered differences refuse measurement. Immediately
before writing a record, every source-library digest (including size-only
subjects) is rechecked beside fixture and Git identity rechecks. A changed
library refuses the write. Failed profiled children report a bounded tail
of collected profiler output alongside native stdout/stderr diagnostics.

Ubuntu x86_64, Rust 1.97.1, GNU BFD ld 2.47, Valgrind 3.27.1, CPU 0. The existing bench rotates four arms, discards two warm-ups and measures twenty native rounds per profile, with private library/user copies on ext4. Cold proof applies to library pages only. The PR wall-time table reports the warm median through first candidate; DHAT reports whole-process allocated bytes and peak heap for that lifecycle. Each value and ratio comes from this one job.

Reproduction uses the existing teardown-provisioned phrases/journals profiles and bisect worker. DATA is the verified BDB data tree with identity `1fbfb06ac394dc51babb59ae72b230cf5ff0d9b9b2744c44c69b7b7c61cd628c`; BASE_TREE is a clean checkout at `01475357`, and PR is the final ordered install. KC_BASE/KC_PR and TK_BASE/TK_PR are the corresponding six-library shipping installs. REG is an ignored private run input. Run record mode, then the measurement command with the same common arguments:

```sh
bench=(uv run --no-project --managed-python python tools/measure-function-order.py
  --subject "base=$BASE" --subject "pr=$PR" --subject "control=$PR" --subject "pin=$PIN"
  --subject "kc-base=$KC_BASE" --subject "kc-pr=$KC_PR"
  --subject "tkrzw-base=$TK_BASE" --subject "tkrzw-pr=$TK_PR"
  --bisect "$BISECT" --system-dir "$DATA" --system-identity "$DATA_ID"
  --profiles-dir "$PROFILES" --work-dir "$WORK" --cpu 0 --rounds 20
  --base-checkout "$BASE_TREE"
  --function-order "base/pinyin=$BASE_TREE/tools/packaging/function-order/bdb/libpinyin.order"
  --function-order "base/zhuyin=$BASE_TREE/tools/packaging/function-order/bdb/libzhuyin.order"
  --function-order "kc-base/pinyin=$BASE_TREE/tools/packaging/function-order/kc/libpinyin.order"
  --function-order "kc-base/zhuyin=$BASE_TREE/tools/packaging/function-order/kc/libzhuyin.order"
  --function-order "tkrzw-base/pinyin=$BASE_TREE/tools/packaging/function-order/tkrzw/libpinyin.order"
  --function-order "tkrzw-base/zhuyin=$BASE_TREE/tools/packaging/function-order/tkrzw/libzhuyin.order")
just heavy -- "${bench[@]}" --record-registration "$REG"
just heavy -- "${bench[@]}" --registration "$REG"
```

### Exact-count interpretation

The retained first-candidate PR/control Ir pairs are 445,660/445,823
(pinyin/phrases), 445,577/445,371 (pinyin/journals), 436,108/435,839
(zhuyin/phrases), and 435,206/436,067 (zhuyin/journals). All combined
startup and steady-Ir controls are also nonexact. Zhuyin/phrases load+init
is 9,483,091 versus 9,483,092. These scopes are INVALID under the exact-count
rule in [packaging](../packaging.md); no ratio, gain or regression follows
from them. The other three load+init scopes have exact controls. No retry
was made. Native observation comparability and allocation/peak-heap control
equality are separate checks and passed.

### Retained symbol-size inspection

The inspection compares the same unstripped base and PR shipping libraries
used by the retained one-run size table. It executes no workload, relink,
strip or benchmark. For each backend and facade:

```sh
nm --defined-only --size-sort --format=posix --demangle=rust "$BASE_SO"
nm --defined-only --size-sort --format=posix --demangle=rust "$PR_SO"
size -A -d "$BASE_SO"
size -A -d "$PR_SO"
readelf -SW "$PR_SO"
```

Sum defined nonzero `T/t/W/w` function bodies after coalescing aliases by
(address, size), normalizing Rust hash suffixes for cross-build names.
Compare the `.text` section separately: its uncovered/alignment residual
is not assigned to named functions. Unwind, relocation and read-only data
section changes also contribute, and ELF section/segment alignment means
the stripped file delta is not the function-size delta. The stripped byte
counts are reused from the retained benchmark; they were not remeasured.

The dominant additions are `core::slice::sort::stable::quicksort::quicksort`
and `core::slice::sort::stable::drift::sort`, instantiated separately by
`Trellis::tails` for `Value`, `rank_candidates` for `(RankKey, usize)`,
and `sort_predicted` for `Predicted`. The last exists only in libpinyin.
Their element layouts and comparison fields differ; the inspected growth
does not expose an identical duplicated instantiation to remove. A shared
index/erased representation would change storage or add indirection, rather
than remove an obvious duplicate. No production change was made.
`candidate_scores` replaces `candidate_frequencies`; treating the renamed
function's whole size as growth would be wrong. Removed heap and GLib merge
instantiations and the smaller n-best/prediction callers offset new bodies.
Named sizes and per-backend totals remain in the PR.

## Exact source-derived witness

The new case imports 龘, 龘甲 and 龘乙 with counts 1/1/2. The first is the prefix, while the two suffixes have unigrams 3/6 and equal displayed lengths. Model20's loaded default-library total is 51,051,831 (the four SubPhraseIndex payload totals 49,150,738 / 27,191 / 1,872,901 / 1,001, read at offset 8 of their MemoryChunk files). With lambda 0.999999, both scaled keys truncate to zero. Token order therefore gives 甲 then 乙 at the pin; the actual scores give 乙 then 甲 in Rust.


The extended frequency cases retain exact observations for both dynamic-adjust
states, imported/system candidates, signed and out-of-range scores, lambda
rounding, and predicted rows. The list permutations follow the same score
conversion removal. `predicted-unigram-overflow` selects the first qualifying
predicted row by rank, not a fixed underlying phrase token; its suffix lookup
filter does not establish the selected full phrase's library. A ranking change
therefore changes which phrase's counter is repeatedly credited. Its observed
acceptance count (264 at the pin, the 1000-call cap in Rust) is recorded exactly.
The 483-count update and the item/sub-index overflow guards at
`pinyin.cpp:2591-2613` are unchanged; this record does not alter those guards.
All original result fields and diagnostics are retained in the policy block.
